item.title: Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain
item.description:
Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain

While working on the Easy Breadcrumb module for Drupal, I came across a situation where a test was failling on Gitlab but was passing with DDev: https://www.drupal.org/project/easy_breadcrumb/issues/3615550

The difference that mattered was that Gitlab serves the site from http://localhost/web for testing and locally it gets served from a fully qualified domain name, ie. http://ddev.site.example.com.

Getting the test to fail locally

Using firecow/gitlab-ci-local

To get the test to fail locally, I used the suggestions at https://project.pages.drupalcode.org/gitlab_templates/info/test-locally/ , which suggested firecow/gitlab-ci-local . I did get that working but I ran into a hitch. My work computer is a Mac with an ARM64 chip and gitlab-ci-local tries to install selenium/standalone-chrome:127.0, which doesn't support ARM64. I dug around and figured out that I could use selenium/standalone-chromium:latest instead by adding a few lines in .gitlab-ci.yml:

phpunit:
  services:
    - !reference [.with-database]
    - name: selenium/standalone-chromium:latest
      alias: selenium
      
# The lines below are to filter which tests run. In this case, only tests in the
# "redirect" group.
variables:
  _PHPUNIT_TESTGROUPS: "redirect"

Then, on the command line, to just run PHPUnit and not most of the other steps, I used the --stage flag to just run jobs in the test stage, which by default is just PHPUnit:

$ drupal-ci-local --stage=test

That worked and I was able to reproduce locally. But, it took about a minute to run the test instead of 2 or 3 seconds with DDev.

Using DDEV to serve a Drupal site from a subdirectory instead of a subdomain

This way is not perfect, but it worked well enough for me to use Xdebug when running tests and when browing the site in a browser.

The code below results in the site being served from a subdirectory named easy, ie. http://example.com/easy.

First, cd to root of project, then:

mkdir router
ls -s ./web ./router/easy

Then, in .ddev/config.yaml

docroot: router

Next, in settings.php

if (isset($GLOBALS['request'])) {
 $request = $GLOBALS['request'];
 $script_name = $request->server->get('SCRIPT_NAME');
 if ($script_name === '/easy/index.php' || $script_name === '/index.php') {
   $request->server->set('SCRIPT_NAME', '/easy/index.php');
 }
}

Then, in .ddev/nginx_full/nginx-site.conf, replace the section that starts with 'location /' to be like this instead:

   # 1. CSS/JS caches
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/(css|js)/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
       expires max;
       log_not_found off;
   }
   # 2. Image styles
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/styles/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
   }
   # 3. Clean URLs
   location /easy {
       try_files $uri $uri/ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }
   # 4. Fallback
   location @rewrite {
       rewrite ^/easy/(.*)$ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }

To run phpunit tests, pass in SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL.
Example which just runs ones test:

ddev exec SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost/easy vendor/bin/phpunit --bootstrap web/core/tests/bootstrap.php --filter testEasyBreadcrumbFollowRedirects web/modules/custom/easy_breadcrumb

item.title: About
item.description:
About

Hi, I'm Brooke :) Nice to meet you or maybe I already know you?

My favorites in life: people, animals, wildlife, science, philosophy, and music. I've always been curious about the nature of things in general.

I was born in 1977 in Wisconsin and moved to California in 1987, where I live today.

My current life

Lately I've been fascinated with the movie Wisdom of Happiness.

I work a lot with Drupal.

I love hanging out with my cat, Luna.

My past

I was born in January 1977 and grew up in a small town of about 4000 people till I was ten years old. My parents moved us to California for jobs.

After high school, I went to Europe for a couple of months. Then to UCSB in 1995, where I was supposed to learn microbiology and get a general education but instead I became fascinated with the internet and learned how to code websites. I've been making websites either full-time or part-time since then, even when working other jobs.

But I couldn't decide on a direction to take at the university. I made a wild decision to go to music school in Hollywood at the Musicians Instititute of Technology where I first learned about digital audio mastering and mixing. After that I did community college in Riverside, CA and eventually moved to Santa Rosa, a quieter town just an hour's drive North of San Francisco.

I worked a ton of odds jobs, played some music, and hung out at the college coffee shop a lot. I did a lot of web work for local businesses. Then in 2011, I met my ex-wife on a radio show and moved to her town. That's when I started doing computer programming full time and specializing in enterprise Drupal for work. I spent over a decade making complex websites for some of the biggest companies in the world.

But COVID happened and I got it really bad with pneumonia and bronchitis in March of 2020. I almost died, I'd say. It took a couple of years to really recover. Work was very difficult. I became quite exhausted, as did a lot of people. Then, in the span of a year in 2023, my cat died and my wife left me, despite me trying very hard to keep the marriage going. I was devastated. I took time off from full-time work to focus on personal healing.

I rescued a new cat, Luna <3. I worked at the animal shelter. I travelled to Europe to see a friend who was feeling down. I read a ton of books. I wrote so much in personal journals. I meditated. Now I've had a few of years to really think about life and what I want to do with the rest of mine. I'm turning 50 this year.

I'm ready to go again, stronger than ever. I'm excited about the future. I'm hopeful and determined. When I work nowadays, I do it happily. Maybe I'll blog about some of it here. I don't know.

Random list of things I've done:

a lot of construction, computer programmer, dirt bikes, play musical instruments, read tons of books, snowboard and ski, mountain bike, fish, disc golf, Tae Kwon Do, audio engineering, co-founded a record label, swim laps, high dives, bungee jump, skateboard (street and some ramps), try to befriend every animal, meditate, camp, study religion, follow politics, work in a factory doing science stuff, drive taxi, work at a automotive transaxle shop, work in a VHS movie rental store, work at In-N-Out Burger, work as a barista, be married, be divorced, care for an elderly woman with dementia, work as an activities coordinator for autistic adults, run cross-country, surf (boards and body), sing solos in choir, tutor Trigonometry, beatbox, almost die from Pneumonia from COVID, play racing video games and Minecraft, read every Terry Goodkind book, medical imaging, 3D animation, study at University of California Santa Barbara and a dozen other community colleges, take everything apart as a kid to find out how stuff works, hang out at coffee shops, and rock climb.

item.title: Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome
item.description:
Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome

This website is made with Drupal. Local development is done with DDEV configured to use Orbstack for container management. The Tome Drupal module exports the dynamic site to a static site. Python is used to preview the site locally. Public hosting is provided free by Github.

Here are some custom bash aliases and functions I use to make common local tasks easy. Concurrently is used to run two processes in one terminal session.

alias brookemahoneycomCd='cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom'
brookemahoneycomLaunch () {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd drupal
  ddev launch
}

brookemahoneycomPreview () {
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd docs
  concurrently 'python -m http.server' 'open "http://localhost:8000"'
}

brookemahoneycomBuild() {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  # Changes to the drupal directory.
  cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal
  # Clears caches.
  ddev drush cr
  # Exports the site with Tome.
  ddev drush tome:static --uri=https://brookemahoney.com
  # Removes old docs directory.
  rm -rf ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies the Tome build directory to docs for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal/html ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies over static files, such as CNAME for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/projects/brookemahoneycom/sync/ ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
}

All the code for the Drupal install is in this site's Github repo.
